newsitem.title: USA: US W Coast prods steady despite Tosco Rodeo glitch.
newsitem.headline: US W Coast prods steady despite Tosco Rodeo glitch.

text.p: U.S. West Coast refined product prices were steady in early talk Thursday despite news that Tosco was forced to shut a hydrocracker after a mishap at its new Rodeo refinery east of San Francisco, traders said.
"Tosco actually came out as a seller of gasoline this morning," said one trader, who noted the news did not change the slack tone of the market in the early going.

Tosco earlier said the coking and hydrocracking units at the 104,000 barrel per day refinery were running at minimal levels after a gas leak hit the desulphurization unit causing smelly, but largely inconsequential releases into the air.
Air quality regulators said the stinky releases of hydrogen sulphide and sulphur dioxide caused as many as 60 complaints overnight, but were not of any long-term concern.
Tosco officials were not immediately available to comment on the operations at the refinery, but traders did not appear the least bit concerned.
CARB cleaner-burning gasoline in Los Angeles remained pegged at between 71 and 72 cents a gallon, while CARB-grade low sulphur diesel remained at between 72 and 73 cents.
